text:
Son of the earth,

the Garden cast you out.

Though you see shadows,

do not seek to shine.


Your mother was beautiful;

the winds dry her out.

Your mother was tender;

she burns in the wasteland.


Your mother was biting

the apple tree’s flower

when man placed

your life in her hand.


Your mother sowed

the rye with you

while you drank

the milk from her bowl.


Son of the wrath

of implacable God.

Your mother cannot save you

from hatred.


Do not sleep, keep watch.

Do not sleep, awaken.

Cold, the barren inheritance

threatens you.


Eyes pursue you

without sweet respite.

The Creator’s eternal hand

hates you.


The gazelles run:

you will run faster.

The lions leap:

you must leap.


The streams flee:

you have to flee.

Though I wish it otherwise,

you cannot sleep!


Do not sleep, listen.

Do not sleep, lie in wait.

The birds will whistle

over drunken branches


to make this dark earth

light for you.

Listen to me, son:

do not sleep, do not sleep…


For all the ages,

do not sleep,

do not sleep!

translation.title: Song to the Firstborn Son
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The Edenic imagery, maternal address, imperative refrain, and stark alternation of tenderness and threat are preserved.
